facts.statement: Alfred S. Romer named a second species, Lagosuchus lilloensis, in 1972 based on larger and better-preserved fossils.
facts.quote: In 1972 he named a second species, Lagosuchus lilloensis, known from larger and more well-preserved specimens.

facts.statement: In 1975, Jose Bonaparte considered Lagosuchus to be intermediate between pseudosuchians and saurischian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: A later review by Jose Bonaparte in 1975 synonymized the two species and considered Lagosuchus intermediate between "pseudosuchians" and saurischian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: In 1994, Paul Sereno and Andrea Arcucci reclassified Lagosuchus lilloensis as a new genus, Marasuchus, due to the fragmentary nature of the original type species.
facts.quote: Paul Sereno and Andrea Arcucci considered L. talampayensis to be undiagnosable in a 1994 study, and reclassified L. lilloensis as a new genus, Marasuchus.

facts.statement: Federico Agnolin and Martin Ezcurra redescribed the holotype skeleton of Lagosuchus talampayensis in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, PULR 09, the holotype skeleton of L. talampayensis, was redescribed by Federico Agnolin and Martin Ezcurra.

facts.statement: Lagosuchus likely had short forelimbs, long shin bones, and a narrow stance, making it an agile biped adapted for running.
facts.quote: With its short forelimbs, long shin bones, and narrow stance, it was likely an agile biped adapted for running.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul inferred that Lagosuchus was one of the smallest Triassic archosaurs, weighing about 167 grams and similar in size to a weasel or ferret.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul inferred that Lagosuchus was one of the smallest Triassic archosaurs, with a weight of about 167 g, similar in size and ecology to a weasel or ferret.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated that Lagosuchus could have reached a total length of 1.7 feet (51 cm) and weighed between 50 and 500 grams, similar to a pigeon.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz estimated that Lagosuchus could have obtained a total length of 1.7 ft (51 cm) and a weight similar to that of a pigeon (50-500 g).

facts.statement: The radius and ulna of Lagosuchus are thin, simple, and unusually short, measuring only about 65% of the humerus length.
facts.quote: The radius and ulna are thin, simple, and unusually short, only about 65% the length of the humerus.

facts.statement: The tibia and fibula of Lagosuchus were narrow and approximately 10% longer than the femur.
facts.quote: The tibia and fibula were narrow and about 10% longer than the femur.

facts.statement: It is believed that Lagosuchus and Marasuchus were transitional forms between cold-blooded reptiles and warm-blooded dinosaurs.
facts.quote: It is believed that Lagosuchus and Marasuchus were transitional between cold blooded reptiles and warm blooded dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Lagosuchus is known from very incomplete remains, including only one hind limb, a scapula, and vertebrae that can be definitively assigned to the genus.
facts.quote: Lagosuchus es conocido de restos muy incompletos (solo una de las extremidades posteriores, una escápula y vértebras que pueden ser asignados definitivamente a este género).

facts.statement: Features and comparisons with close relatives suggest Lagosuchus could run on its hind legs for brief periods but likely walked on four legs most of the time.
facts.quote: Estos rasgos, así como las comparaciones con sus parientes cercanos, sugieren que podía correr con sus patas traseras por breves períodos, y probablemente caminaría sobre las cuatro la mayor parte del tiempo.

facts.statement: Lagosuchus was probably an agile predator that could use its speed to chase prey and escape from much larger predators.
facts.quote: Lagosuchus era probablemente un ágil depredador que podría usar su velocidad para perseguir a sus presas y escapar de depredadores mucho mayores.

facts.statement: Lagosuchus, meaning "rabbit crocodile" in Greek, is an extinct genus of small archosaurs found in the Middle Triassic (Ladinian stage) of Argentina, about 230 million years ago.
facts.quote: Lagosuchus (griego: "cocodrilo conejo") es un género extinto de pequeños arcosaurios cuyos fósiles fueron hallados en la Formación Chañares de Argentina, que data del Triásico Medio (etapa del Ladiniense), hace unos 230 million years ago.

facts.statement: Lagosuchus is generally considered closely related to dinosaurs as a member of the group Dinosauromorpha.
facts.quote: Se ha considerado generalmente como cercanamente relacionado con los dinosaurios, al ser un miembro del grupo Dinosauromorpha.

facts.statement: The time range for Lagosuchus is estimated from 241.464 to 237 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Ladinian (241.464 to 237 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some paleontologists argue that Lagosuchus is a valid genus and that Marasuchus is a junior synonym of it.
facts.quote: However, other paleontologists support the argument that Lagosuchus is a valid genus, and that Marasuchus is a junior synonym of it.

facts.statement: The age of the Chañares Formation has been the subject of much debate.
facts.quote: The Chañares Formation's age has been through much debate.
